cover.text: Rep. Josh Gottheimer wants the NSA to test AI models before release.

slides.headline: Two bipartisan AI bills unveiled Friday
slides.body: On September 18, Rep. Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) unveiled two bipartisan AI security bills at Fairleigh Dickinson University in Teaneck.

slides.quote: Right now, there are no mandatory requirements for pre-deployment testing of frontier AI models.

slides.headline: The NSA would get 30 days to vet a model
The FIREWALL Act would extend that ban
slides.body: DeepSeek is already blocked from federal devices. Gottheimer named Kimi K3 and Qwen as Chinese open-weight models the bill would also keep off federal systems.

slides.headline: He's also pressing the Cyber Director
slides.note: Letter to Cyber Director on AI cyberattacks
slides.body: Gottheimer said he's writing to Sean Cairncross, the President's Cyber Director, asking whether the Administration's new AI cybersecurity clearinghouse is built for today's threats.

slides.note: Gottheimer said Republican leadership sent Congress home without acting on any of these critical pieces of legislation.

caption:
Rep. Josh Gottheimer introduced two bipartisan AI security bills at Fairleigh Dickinson University on September 18. The American AI Security Act, co-led with Rep. Mike Lawler, would require mandatory NSA reviews of the most powerful AI models before companies release them, giving the agency 30 days with a possible 30-day extension. The China FIREWALL Act, co-led with Rep. Nick LaLota, would ban Chinese-developed open-weight AI models from federal devices and software. Gottheimer named Kimi K3 and Qwen as models still on federal systems. He is also sending a letter to National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross about the administration’s AI cybersecurity clearinghouse.

Gottheimer said Republican leadership has refused to directly bring these bills to the floor for a vote, and he is urging the Speaker to reconvene Congress before the election.
